title: ZIP Code Boundary Viewer: Postal Context
description: Read which ZIP or postcode applies to a point with the ZIP Code Boundary Viewer — postal fields and nearby postal context. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a point near a ZIP edge shows its own code plus the neighbours across the line — the context that explains a surprising delivery route in one view.
quick_answer: The ZIP Code Boundary Viewer finds which ZIP or postcode applies to a point and shows the related nearby postal context. Locate the point and read the postal fields — an honest point-level read that keeps ZIP geography in its delivery-route nature, distinct from the Census's statistical areas.

body.t: Two parcels across a street can carry different codes — routes serve efficiency, not symmetry. The viewer's nearby context shows the line's neighbourhood instead of pretending the point's answer is the whole story.
Some ZIPs are a single facility or a PO Box wall — points, not polygons. The viewer reports the point's postal fields as the record holds them, routes and all.

faq: For US ZIPs there is no official USPS polygon to be exact with — ZIPs are delivery routes. The viewer reports the point's applicable code and nearby context; Census ZCTA boundaries (the statistical polygons) live on the What ZIP Code Am I In page.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — locate any point by search or click.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Commercial ZIP maps approximate route geography differently; two 'ZIP boundary' products can disagree while both approximate the same routes.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
The viewer reads postcode fields internationally where the data supports it — UK outward districts and full postcodes in their own structure.
Which code for a brand-new development?
New addresses can precede postal updates; USPS's own lookup is the freshest source during the gap.
A point with two plausible codes?
Edges do that — the nearby context shows both candidates and their relation to the point; the address's official USPS record decides mail.
Census ZCTA shapefiles are the downloadable official geography (from the Census). Route-based ZIP shapes are commercial approximations.
Common and workable with this caveat in the plan: codes change with mail's needs, so territories built on them need periodic re-reads — this viewer is the re-read.
